blogs.title: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026: From user to contributor to maintainer
blogs.content: Posted on October 1, 2026 by epower You do not need “maintainer” in your job title to start following the maintainer journey at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 . You might be an SRE who has spent years operating a CNCF project in production. An application developer who found and fixed a bug. An infrastructure engineer who has opened issues, improved documentation, or built something your upstream community could use. KubeCon + CloudNativeCon gives attendees several ways to move closer to the open source communities behind the technology, whether you are already a maintainer or are making your first contribution. Register Today ! Why maintainers and future contributors should attend For existing maintainers, KubeCon + CloudNativeCon creates rare face-to-face time with contributors, users, and neighboring project communities. Those conversations can surface real-world feedback, new contributors, shared technical challenges, and opportunities to collaborate across the ecosystem. For attendees who are not maintainers yet, the event provides multiple low-barrier ways to get closer to a project. Maintainer Track sessions , ContribFests , Project Lightning Talks , and the Project Pavilion can help turn “I use this project” into “I know how to contribute to it.” Come with a community challenge or a curiosity If you already maintain a project, think about the challenge that is hardest to solve asynchronously: contributor onboarding, release processes, project governance, documentation, adoption feedback, or collaboration across projects. Face-to-face time can make those conversations much easier. If you are newer to contribution, your questions may be simpler: Which project community matches the technologies or problems I care about? Where could someone with my skills make a useful first contribution? How do contributors move from a first issue or pull request into deeper project involvement? What do maintainers wish more users understood about participating in their projects? Already a maintainer? Start Sunday For eligible CNCF project maintainers, the CNCF Maintainer Summit takes place on Sunday, November 8 before the main conference. The Summit provides a dedicated space for the people behind CNCF projects to meet face-to-face, share best practices, discuss contribution processes, and work through common challenges across project communities. Separate registration and eligibility requirements apply, so attendees should review those requirements ahead of time. Monday: See what projects are building On Monday, Project Lightning Talks give CNCF projects five minutes each to share recent updates, new features, and other highlights. Unlike the CNCF-hosted co-located events, Project Lightning Talks are available with any in-person KubeCon + CloudNativeCon pass. For someone exploring the ecosystem, this is a fast way to discover projects you may not already know. For existing contributors and maintainers, it is a chance to see what neighboring communities are working on. Tuesday through Thursday: Go behind the project The Maintainer Track is where attendees can hear directly from CNCF project maintainers about new developments, technical challenges, implementation considerations, community priorities, and project roadmaps. Sessions to consider include: Kubernetes SIG ContribEx: Sub-Project and Governance Updates Kubernetes SIG Architecture Intro and Updates TAG DevEx State of the Union: What We’re Shipping and Why It Matters Built for What’s Next: Backstage’s Role in AI-Assisted Development Maintainer sessions from projects including Harbor, Flux, Cilium, etcd, Linkerd, OpenCost, KubeVirt, and many others If there is a project your organization depends on, this is an opportunity to hear from and talk with the people building it. Make your first contribution ContribFests turn that conversation into hands-on participation. Attendees can work alongside project maintainers and contributors to tackle real issues, learn contribution workflows, understand project architecture, and begin participating in a community. This year’s program includes opportunities with communities including: OpenTelemetry Harbor Podman Backstage Argo CD Meshery Inspektor Gadget Some sessions explicitly welcome first-time contributors. You do not have to arrive knowing exactly how you want to contribute. Showing up curious is enough to start. Visit the Project Pavilion The Project Pavilion is open during the main conference in the Solutions Showcase and provides another easy way to connect directly with project communities. Stop by a project kiosk. Ask maintainers what they are working on. Find out where they need help. Discover a project you did not know existed. Sometimes the path into open source starts with a pull request. Sometimes it starts with a hallway conversation. Don’t schedule every minute For maintainers and future contributors, some of the most valuable parts of the week may never appear on the formal schedule. A conversation at a project kiosk can turn into end-user feedback. A ContribFest introduction can become a first pull request. A hallway discussion can connect two projects working through the same problem. Use the scheduled programming as a starting point, but leave room for the community around it. Those relationships are often what continue long after the conference ends. What you can take back to your project or community For maintainers, the value can be practical: new contributor relationships, direct end-user feedback, ideas borrowed from other project communities, and time to solve problems that are difficult to work through in issues and chat. For future contributors, you may leave with: A clearer understanding of where your skills fit in the CNCF ecosystem A first contribution, issue, or community connection to continue after the event A better understanding of project roadmaps, governance, and contributor pathways Relationships with maintainers and contributors who can help turn curiosity into ongoing participation Maintainers can come from anywhere That is why the Maintainer Journey overlaps every other journey in this series. SREs bring production experience. Application developers understand how projects feel to the people building with them. Infrastructure engineers understand what happens when those projects have to operate at scale. Open source communities need all of those perspectives. Whether you already maintain a CNCF project, have made a few contributions, or are simply wondering how to get involved, KubeCon + CloudNativeCon gives you a place to take the next step. Join us in Salt Lake City and find your place in the cloud native community. Don’t forget to register for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026. Share

blogs.title: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026: Build your infrastructure engineer journey
blogs.content: Posted on October 1, 2026 by CNCF Marketing Team Infrastructure engineers sit at one of the busiest intersections in cloud native. Kubernetes clusters need to scale. Networks need to connect them. Storage needs to follow workloads. Platforms need to make infrastructure usable. Security needs to be built in. And increasingly, infrastructure teams are also being asked to support GPU-intensive, AI, and agentic workloads. That means your KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 journey is unlikely to stay inside one track. Expect to move between Platform Engineering, Operations + Performance, Connectivity, Data Processing + Storage, Security, AI Infrastructure, and Maintainer Track sessions throughout the week. View the tracks + schedule . Register Today ! Why infrastructure engineers should attend Infrastructure teams are being asked to support more types of workloads, more clusters, more automation, and increasingly GPU and AI infrastructure without giving up reliability, security, or cost control. KubeCon + CloudNativeCon brings those challenges together across platform engineering, networking, storage, operations, security, and AI infrastructure. For infrastructure engineers, the value is the chance to compare architectures and operating models with peers, hear how other organizations are solving production problems at scale, and talk directly with the maintainers building the projects underneath their platforms. Come with an architecture decision in mind Infrastructure engineers are rarely evaluating technology in the abstract. There is usually a platform decision, scaling challenge, migration, cost constraint, or new workload driving the conversation. Bring one of those decisions with you and use the week to pressure-test it. Questions worth bringing include: Where is your current platform reaching its limits? Which decisions around networking, storage, identity, or multi-cluster operations are becoming harder to manage? How will GPU-intensive, inference, or agentic workloads change the infrastructure you already operate? What should your platform automate, and what should remain visible to the teams using it? Use Monday to pick a specialty If you want to attend Monday’s CNCF-hosted co-located events, choose an All-Access Pass; the KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Only Pass does not include them. Infrastructure engineers have several strong options among Monday’s CNCF-hosted co-located events. Platform Engineering Day focuses on the real-world challenges of building and scaling internal developer platforms. CiliumCon goes deeper into cloud native networking, observability, and security using Cilium, Hubble, Tetragon, and eBPF. OpenTofu Day is a natural destination for infrastructure-as-code practitioners. And FluxCon provides another path for teams operating GitOps-based infrastructure and continuous delivery environments. Your challenge may be choosing just one. Follow the infrastructure lifecycle During the main conference, look for sessions that connect architecture decisions with the reality of operating infrastructure at scale. Consider adding sessions such as: When Infrastructure Breaks in Production: How EarnIn Brought Testing to the Full CNCF Stack The New Scaling Matrix: Balancing In-Place Resizing, VPA, HPA and Automation Solutions From Pending Pod to Ready Node: Declarative Worker Images for Kubernetes Scale-Out Zero Downtime CNI Migration at Scale: Canal to Cilium Across Hundreds of Production Clusters Follow the GPUs: How a Regulated Fortune 100 Serves Customers When No Single Cloud Has Enough Many Clusters, One GPU Pool: Locality-Aware Scheduling and Data Delivery With Kueue and Dragonfly RBAC as a Platform Capability: Applying Platform Engineering to Kubernetes Access Together they touch scaling, GitOps, networking, GPU infrastructure, multi-cluster environments, access management, platform reliability, and production operations. Find the projects underneath your platform Infrastructure engineers may want to make time for communities around projects such as Cilium, Flux, Argo, OpenTofu, SPIFFE/SPIRE, Kueue, Dragonfly, etcd, KubeVirt, and others connected to their stack. The Project Pavilion is an especially useful stop. Instead of evaluating a technology through documentation alone, you can talk directly with maintainers about architecture choices, deployment patterns, upcoming features, and the problems you are seeing in production. Follow AI infrastructure without abandoning the fundamentals AI infrastructure is increasingly visible throughout this year’s schedule, from GPU scheduling and inference to networking, storage, observability, and security. For infrastructure engineers, that does not necessarily mean learning an entirely new stack. Many of the same questions still matter: Where does the workload run? How does it scale? How is it secured? How is it observed? What happens when something fails? Use the AI-focused sessions to understand how familiar infrastructure principles are being applied to a new generation of workloads. Don’t schedule every minute Architecture tradeoffs rarely fit neatly into a 35-minute session. Being at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon gives you the chance to continue those conversations with speakers, maintainers, and engineers who have already made similar decisions in production. Leave time to visit the Project Pavilion and Solutions Showcase, compare implementation details, and ask the questions that do not fit on a slide: What broke? What did you change? What would you do differently at twice the scale? What you can take back to your team The value of the week is the ability to compare architecture choices with people who have already tested them in production, including the maintainers building the underlying projects. You may leave with: Reference points for platform, networking, storage, access, and multi-cluster architecture decisions A clearer view of the tradeoffs behind GitOps, autoscaling, infrastructure as code, and platform automation Ideas for supporting AI and GPU workloads without abandoning core reliability and security practices Project roadmap context and peer connections that can inform your next design review or migration Where does the infrastructure journey go next? If reliability and production operations are the biggest part of your role, continue with the SRE Journey. If you spend your time building platforms specifically to improve how developers work, the Application Developer Journey can help you see your platform from the other side. And if you want to influence the infrastructure projects your organization depends on, explore the Maintainer Journey. Join us in Salt Lake City and start planning your path through KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. Don’t forget to register for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026. Share

blogs.title: KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026: Build your application developer journey
blogs.content: Posted on October 1, 2026 by CNCF Marketing Team Cloud native development increasingly means thinking beyond the application itself. How will it be built? How will it be deployed? How much infrastructure should developers need to understand? Where should platforms remove complexity? And what changes when AI agents become part of the development workflow? Application developers will find those questions throughout KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026 . The Application Development + Delivery track is an obvious starting point, but your path may also take you through Platform Engineering, Security, Observability, AI Inference + Agentic, Maintainer Track sessions, and CNCF project communities. View the tracks + schedule . Register Today ! Why application developers should attend Cloud native is increasingly shaping what happens before and after code is written. KubeCon + CloudNativeCon gives application developers a chance to see how developer platforms, delivery workflows, observability, security, and AI-assisted tooling are changing the way applications move from a laptop into production. It is also a chance to meet the communities building the tools developers use every day, understand the infrastructure decisions happening behind the abstractions, and bring a developer perspective into conversations about what the next generation of cloud native platforms should look like. Come with your biggest developer-friction point You do not need to arrive with a perfectly defined cloud native strategy. Start with the part of building and shipping software that feels harder than it should, then use the conference to explore how other teams are approaching it. Ask yourself: Where does your inner development loop slow down? How much infrastructure knowledge do developers on your team need just to ship safely? Where do platform abstractions help, and where do they create new friction? What changes when AI-assisted development or agentic workflows become part of the application lifecycle? Choose your Monday based on what you want to build If you want to attend Monday’s CNCF-hosted co-located events, choose an All-Access Pass ; the KubeCon + CloudNativeCon Only Pass does not include them. For developers focused on developer experience and internal tooling, BackstageCon offers a full day centered on the open source framework for building developer portals. If AI-assisted development is becoming part of your work, Agentics Day: MCP + Agents explores real-world implementations and emerging patterns around agents, tools, data, and Model Context Protocol. And if you spend a lot of time thinking about the relationship between developers and the platforms beneath them, Platform Engineering Day provides another path into developer experience, self-service, and internal developer platforms. There is no single correct choice. Start with the problem closest to your work. Follow the application from laptop to production Across the main conference, developers can explore everything from application architecture and deployment to feature delivery and AI-assisted workflows. Sessions to consider include: Going Cloud Native in Baseball How We Are Enabling Feature Flagging At Scale From Laptop to Cluster: The Agentic AI Inner Loop on Kubernetes Sandboxing on Kubernetes with WebAssembly: A Hands-on Tutorial Not Just for Infrastructure: Rebuilding an OSS Product with Kubernetes-Style Architecture From Vibe to Live: Building for the Real World TAG DevEx State of the Union: What We’re Shipping and Why It Matters The common thread is not simply Kubernetes. It is how developers can build, ship, test, and operate software more effectively using cloud native technologies. Meet the projects shaping the developer experience Build time into your agenda to explore projects including Backstage, Argo, OpenFeature, OpenTelemetry, Podman, and other projects connected to the way your applications are developed and delivered. Maintainer Track sessions can help you understand where projects are heading, while the Project Pavilion gives you an opportunity to ask questions directly. And if you are interested in doing more than using a project, look for a ContribFest . For example, From Curious to Contributor: Ship Your First Backstage PR is designed to help attendees contribute directly with project maintainers. Podman also has a ContribFest welcoming first-time contributors. Look beyond the application One of the benefits of attending KubeCon + CloudNativeCon as an application developer is understanding what happens after your code leaves your laptop. Spend some time in an Observability session. Sit in on a Platform Engineering talk. Learn how infrastructure teams think about reliability, security, resource management, and scale. The better developers and infrastructure teams understand one another, the easier it becomes to build platforms and applications that work well together. Don’t schedule every minute The sessions will give you ideas, but the in-person value is being able to keep the conversation going. Talk with the maintainers behind the tools you use, compare developer experience with other application teams, and spend time with platform engineers to understand why the systems beneath your applications work the way they do. Make room for the Project Pavilion, Solutions Showcase, and informal conversations between sessions. Sometimes the most useful takeaway is not a new tool; it is finding someone who has already solved the developer problem your team is facing. What you can take back to your team A good developer journey should leave you with more than a few new project names. It should give you concrete ideas for making the path from code to production simpler, safer, and easier to understand. You may leave with: Patterns for improving developer experience and reducing cognitive load New approaches to the inner loop, delivery workflows, feature management, and application observability A better understanding of how platform and infrastructure decisions affect developers Projects, maintainers, and communities you can turn to when you want to go deeper Where does the developer journey go next? If you find yourself especially interested in platforms, automation, or developer self-service, explore our Infrastructure Engineer Journey. If you are increasingly interested in the open source projects behind your developer experience, the Maintainer Journey can show you how to move from user to contributor and potentially become part of the community shaping those technologies. Join us in Salt Lake City and build your own path through KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America. Don’t forget to register for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026. Share
